summary: Claude Code (hyperpowers) correctly escalated the ambiguous "add logging" brief to the architectural path: it invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming, announced "Classification: architectural", ran a multi-section design dialogue, wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-logging-subsystem-design.md, presented it for review with no implementation code written, and only began implementation planning after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are supported by directly observed screen text, the on-disk spec file, git status, and session-log grep. The only anomaly (broken Codex stub review gate) did not block the brainstorming flow but is worth an engineer's attention.

observations.description: Codex spec-review gate failed silently-ish: agent reported "One round, both spec lenses (completeness-and-consistency, feasibility-and-scope) returned an empty {} payload. verdict-normalize --require-coverage returned incomplete for both ... status --json shows no jobs at all (running: [], recent: []) ... that's a non-functional companion". Runtime reported as codex-plugin-cc 0.0.0-stub with no config.toml at $CODEX_HOME. The spec was handed over without the independent second review.

On the first AskUserQuestion prompt I typed "5" (the "Type something." option) as a chat message; it was recorded as "User declined to answer questions" rather than opening a free-text field. Answering in the following chat turn worked, but the decline framing is misleading.
Long stretches (up to ~6m24s "Cogitated") with a static screen; nothing indicated a subagent/Codex gate was running until the final hand-back block appeared.
Spec front matter says "Status: approved design, pending implementation plan" even though it was written before the human approved it — slightly presumptuous wording at the moment of writing.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: `"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"` appears before `hyperpowers:writing-plans` in the JSONL under home/.claude/projects/.../*.jsonl

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. 'Logging' here is a new subsystem this repo doesn't have ... I'll go through the full process: questions, approaches, a design you approve section by section, then a written spec." File on disk: coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-logging-subsystem-design.md (ls output)

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-logging-subsystem-design.md (not committed) ... Please review it and tell me if you want changes before I move to the implementation plan." `git status --short` in workdir at that point showed only `?? docs/` — no source files modified.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Agent explicitly said "Classification: architectural" and produced a spec file; no in-chat-only bounded design occurred.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe or throwaway spike plan appeared on screen; the flow went design questions → spec doc → approval → hyperpowers:writing-plans skill.
